findings.current_drug_context: Type 2 diabetes (12 yrs) managed on metformin and gliclazide (a sulfonylurea). Established cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. No SGLT2 inhibitor prescribed. Last medication review 2019.
findings.drift: Margaret has established cardiovascular disease AND chronic kidney disease but is not on an SGLT2 inhibitor. Current guidance recommends one for cardiorenal protection, independent of blood-sugar control. Her regimen predates that guidance and has not been revisited since 2019.

eligibility.reasoning: Type 2 diabetes with established CVD and CKD — both qualifying indications. eGFR is 46 mL/min/1.73m², above the initiation threshold. The indication is independent of glycaemic control, so HbA1c 58 mmol/mol does not change eligibility.

contraindication_check.notes: No documented SGLT2-inhibitor hypersensitivity. No history of recurrent genital or urinary infection on record. Not on insulin, so DKA risk is low. eGFR 46 is above the initiation threshold. No contraindication identified.

items.label: Established CVD
items.detail: On record as a qualifying indication.

items.label: Chronic kidney disease
items.detail: On record as a qualifying indication.

items.label: Diagnosis codes present
items.detail: Type 2 diabetes, CVD and CKD all coded in the record.

items.label: Glucose-lowering effect is modest at this eGFR
items.detail: Below eGFR ~45 the glucose-lowering effect falls away — but initiation here is for cardiorenal protection, not glycaemic control, so this is not a reason to withhold.

items.label: Volume status / diuretics
items.detail: Not on a high-dose diuretic; low hypotension risk on initiation.

items.label: Type 1 diabetes / DKA risk
items.detail: Type 2 diabetes, not on insulin — euglycaemic DKA risk is low.

items.label: Frailty / age 68
items.detail: No frailty flags on record; counsel on sick-day rules as below.

items.label: Sulfonylurea (gliclazide) — hypo risk
items.detail: Adding an SGLT2 inhibitor can increase hypoglycaemia risk; consider reducing the gliclazide dose.

items.label: Sick-day rules
items.detail: Pause during acute dehydrating illness; restart when eating and drinking normally.

items.label: Euglycaemic DKA warning
items.detail: Seek help for nausea, vomiting or breathlessness even if blood sugars look normal.

items.label: Genital/urinary hygiene
items.detail: Advise on hygiene and to report symptoms of infection.

items.label: Fournier's gangrene safety-net
items.detail: Rare; safety-net for severe genital pain, swelling or redness with fever.

items.label: Expected early eGFR dip is NOT a reason to stop
items.detail: A small initial fall in eGFR is expected and reversible — do not discontinue for it.

items.label: No routine post-initiation renal/potassium monitoring required
items.detail: Over-monitoring is a barrier, not a safeguard; routine bloods are not needed for this indication.

findings.recommended_action: Initiate an SGLT2 inhibitor for cardiorenal protection alongside current therapy. Consider reducing the sulfonylurea dose. Counsel on sick-day rules and genital hygiene.
findings.patient_explanation: The guidance for people with your combination of diabetes, heart, and kidney history has been updated. There is now a type of tablet that helps protect your heart and kidneys, on top of managing blood sugar — and you are not currently taking it. This is common, and it is not an emergency.
findings.patient_offer: Your prescriber has reviewed your records and thinks a once-daily tablet that helps protect your heart and kidneys could be right for you. It works alongside your current medicines. It's your choice — here's what it does and what to look out for, and you can decide together with your prescriber.
structured_questions: In the last few months, have you had frequent thrush or urinary infections?
Do you ever get lightheaded or dizzy when you stand up?
findings.clinician_summary: 68F, T2DM + established CVD + CKD (eGFR 46), on metformin + sulfonylurea, no SGLT2i. Meets 2023 cardiorenal indication; eGFR above initiation threshold; no contraindication. Consider dose-reducing sulfonylurea. Pack ready to sign.
findings.draft_prescription: Dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily. Reduce gliclazide dose and review hypo risk. Counsel on sick-day rules. No routine renal/potassium recheck required for this indication.
